Definition: probably a contraction from Ὀλυμπιόδωρος (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended); Olympas, a Christian:--Olympas.
BiblicalUsage: Olympas is a Christian at Rome, greeted once in Romans 16:15, where Paul says to salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints with them. He is one of the believers whose only mark is a greeting at the end of a letter.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that a greeting in Romans is a place in the church, and God remembers the saints whose whole story is a single salute.
